P1.evidence: Setter notes read back cleanly: 'I know you had a conversation with Kyla ... I was taking a look at those notes and really just got to pick up where you left off with her.' The frame was two-part, not four — 'to see if what you're looking to achieve is in alignment with what we do' and 'go a bit deeper into some of the challenges with your fitness' — with no 'where you want to go' or 'what you need' element. No explicit 'does that work?'; the prospect volunteered 'sounds good'. Open question ran verbatim: 'how can we potentially help?'

P2.evidence: Weight covered ('how much more weight do you feel like you have to go?' → 210 peak, 181 now); age and height never asked. Work covered well including the desk/physical split: 'Is the fabrication work ... very physical?' Health and injuries both asked directly — 'is there any other things that you were dealing with or health issues wise?' and 'Aches or pains or anything like that?' Training week only reached as 'you said you've been doing the kettlebells for like two weeks now?' with no days-per-week figure. Sleep was volunteered unprompted ('I was hungry when I would go to bed ... I slept horribly') and never asked. Energy never raised.

P3.evidence: Aesthetics probed only as a scale-versus-feel question: 'is it more just about how you look, how you feel, your aesthetics, rather than a number on the scale?' The can't-do-physically question ran well: 'is there any things that you're wanting to do? Maybe other sports?' → skiing, snowboarding, dancing. The bridge ran: 'was there maybe a moment where you were like, okay, now I have to change ... maybe some bigger reason why you want it' → produced the identity crisis, the failed relationship and the mortgage. But the rep answered that with 'Wow. Okay.' and immediately pivoted to health conditions. 'What does that actually do for you?' and 'Who else does that impact?' never ran — no family, partner or legacy thread was opened at all. The long summary at 00:20:21 restated the situation but never landed the 'this isn't really about the weight' reframe.

P4.evidence: Past attempts surfaced sideways, via 'what was it that drew you towards the older, simpler ways of working out ... why that compared to just, I know you mentioned you don't want to be a bodybuilder' — that is a preference question, not 'what have you tried before'. Most of the history (bodybuilding at 15, calorie logging, fasting, two weeks of self-directed swings) was volunteered, not asked for. The blocker was half-named by the rep off the setter notes — 'you mentioned you had some worries about potential future injuries or doing it properly' — and the prospect named it himself as timidness and 'doing it myself all on by myself'. Never asked why it did not stick, and never ran 'the information isn't the problem — why can't you stick to it on your own?', which was the single most available line on this call.

P5.evidence: The Consequence Frame never ran. No two-year question, no 'is that something you're willing to settle for', no 'why not', no line in the sand. The prospect had handed the rep unusually rich material for it — atrophy, dysmorphia, isolation, 'witnessing yourself partially decompose' — and none of it was pointed forward. This is the phase that would have carried the later money conversation and it was skipped entirely.

P6.evidence: No commitment check before presenting. The nearest attempt was 'just before we go into the investment side of things, how do you feel about all that so far?', which drew 'I'm unsure. I've never done anything like this before. It's hard to imagine what that looks like.' Hesitation surfaced and the rep did not return to Phase 5 — he answered the process question and moved straight to price. The belief question was only asked after the money objection landed ('do you actually feel like ... it would work for you and it would be worth it') — the right question in the wrong phase.

P11.evidence: No close was attempted. Price was presented, the money objection landed, the rep downsold three times and then accepted 'I'm going to do some numbers on my end and get back to you' without ever asking for the sale. Payment, the Trevor onboarding call, the agreement email and the Skool/welcome-email steps were never reached.

objection_plays.detail: Isolation ran and ran well: 'is it literally just the amount' and 'do you actually feel like ... it would work for you and it would be worth it. Is there any doubt about that?' Permission for the financial conversation ran: 'are you open to having a conversation about where you're at financially?' Two of the six financial-picture questions ran — monthly surplus ('how much do you generally have left over at the end of the month') and savings ('do you have any sort of side savings or checkings'). Both came back zero. Credit cards, available credit per card, used-versus-available and investments were never asked. 'You're not in a SHOULD I place, you're in a HOW place' never ran. Critically, the play was abandoned at the first two zeroes and replaced with a descending ladder of cheaper products rather than either a structured plan on the real offer or a clean disqualification.

'I have to like crunch numbers on my end, it's not something I can do in real time' and 'I'm going to do some numbers on my end and get back to you' are a think-about-it in substance. None of the play ran — no 'do you feel what we've gone through CAN get you to your goal', no 'what's actually coming up that's preventing you from getting started', no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is'. The rep replied 'Okay, cool. Well, anything, any other questions for me before we hop off?'

Script gap, not a rep failure. The prospect is not price-resistant, he is genuinely pre-revenue — zero surplus, zero savings, not paying himself, cannot cover his own mortgage. The playbook has no disqualification path for a prospect who wants the programme and demonstrably cannot fund it, so the rep improvised downward through three unpublished price points instead. This is the same shape as the known 'cheaper alternative' gap but the driver is capacity, not perceived value.

notes: Strong rapport and a genuinely good discovery on history and identity, then the two phases that convert — Consequence Frame and Commitment Check — were skipped wholesale, so the price landed with no cost-of-inaction and no verbal yes underneath it. Coach on two things: run P5/P6 before ever saying a number, and qualify affordability before the presentation rather than after the objection, which would have saved forty minutes and prevented the improvised discounting.
